gpsr-setup-generator-form: Sec. 2.1, p.3: the paper derives the Fourier-series form of E(x) (Eq. 6) for U(x)=exp(ixG) by expanding in the eigenbasis of G. The value is that derived result, not an experimental setup.
gpsr-full-reconstruction-2r-plus-1: Sec. 3.1, p.5: 2R+1 unknown coefficients are fixed by 2R+1 equations at distinct points (a DFT); the value carries the equidistant integer-frequency condition from the Sec. 3 preface. A derivation in the text, no numbered theorem.
gpsr-odd-part-2r-evals: Sec. 3.2, p.5: R unknown coefficients b_l, R equations at R points, each E_odd evaluation costs two E evaluations. Derived in the text; the paper itself notes the saved E(0) evaluation is used anyway.
gpsr-even-part-2r-evals: Sec. 3.3, p.5-6: R+1 evaluations of E_even; periodicity for integer frequencies (Eqs. 21-23) gives 2R evaluations of E. Derived in the text with the integer condition.
gpsr-resource-measures-defined: Sec. 2.3, p.4: the paper defines N_eval and the total shot count N as its two comparison measures.
gpsr-constant-variance-assumption: Sec. 2.3, p.4 and footnote 4: the paper states the constant one-shot variance approximation and calls it potentially very rough.
gpsr-decomposition-circuit-count: Sec. 3.5.1, p.6: 2P circuits for the first derivative by the two-term rule on P gates; 2P^2-P+1 for the second via the full Hessian of the elementary gates (App. A.4.2). A counting argument for the decomposition method, with its setting stated.
gpsr-hessian-diagonal-evals: Sec. 4.1, p.8-9: 2R_k evaluations per diagonal entry as a univariate restriction; 2(R_k+R_m)-1 for an off-diagonal entry given the diagonal and E(x0). Derived in the text with the equidistant condition.
gpsr-hessian-offdiagonal-frequencies: Sec. 4.1, p.8 and App. A.2, p.18: the restriction E^(km) is a Fourier series with R_k+R_m equidistant frequencies, derived in App. A.2 for integer-valued frequencies.
gpsr-qaoa-frequency-bound-needed: Sec. 5.1, p.10-11: the paper states that knowing all QAOA frequencies needs the full spectrum of H_P, so upper bounds must be used and R may be overestimated.
gpsr-qaoa-fig3-setup: Fig. 3 caption, p.12: the paper states the setup of its numerical comparison (n=6 parameters, MaxCut graphs).
gpsr-rotosolve-noninteger-cost: Sec. 5.2, p.12: the paper states that the cost is typically significantly increased for noninteger frequencies.
gpsr-qad-open-benefit: Sec. 5.3, p.13: the paper states it is still to be investigated whether the extension gives better optimization, and that Fig. 4 uses toy circuits.
